intro: Weddings, traditions, fun customs, and the vocabulary of a popular festival.

disfrazarse de.nota: Use de before the character or costume: disfrazarse de pirata.

la despedida de soltero.nota: Use despedida de soltero for a groom and despedida de soltera for a bride; names and customs vary by region.

envolver.nota: The stem changes from o to ue in forms such as envuelvo, but not in envolvemos.

animado.nota: The adjective agrees with the noun: animado, animada, animados, animadas.

tradicional.nota: Same form for masculine and feminine: un baile tradicional, una comida tradicional.

participar.nota: Participar en un concurso: take part in a contest.

soler.en: to usually do; to tend to
soler.nota: Soler is followed by an infinitive: se suele bailar (people usually dance).

martes y trece.nota: In Spain, this date is traditionally associated with bad luck; beliefs vary.

es costumbre que.nota: When followed by a clause with a different subject, use the subjunctive: es costumbre que los vecinos cenen.

bloques.texto:
Many towns in Spain celebrate local **fiestas populares**; some have **un concurso** or a night **verbena**. Events may include **un desfile** with **carrozas**, **música**, **fuegos artificiales** or food in the street. During **Carnaval**, people **se disfrazan de** different characters. Customs vary from place to place.

At a wedding, there may be **la despedida de soltero/a**, **la boda**, **el banquete** and **la luna de miel**. You **felicitas a** the couple: **¡Enhorabuena! ¡Que seáis muy felices!** In Spain, **seáis** addresses **vosotros**; in much of Latin America, people use **ustedes**: **¡Que sean muy felices!**

Presents: **envolver** a gift, **abrirlo** or **hacer un regalo**.

At a festival: **ir a la verbena**, **participar** en un concurso, an **animado** or **tradicional** ambiente. In Spain, some people associate **martes y trece** with bad luck.

Talk about customs with **soler + infinitive**, impersonal **se suele + infinitive**, **es costumbre + infinitive** or **es costumbre que + subjunctive**: **Se suele** cenar tarde; **es costumbre** dar dos besos; **es costumbre que los vecinos cenen juntos**; **es típico** bailar.

frases.es: Cada agosto mi pueblo celebra sus fiestas, que duran una semana.
frases.en: Every August my village celebrates its annual festivities, which last a week.

frases.es: El primer día hay un desfile y los niños se disfrazan.
frases.en: On the first day there is a parade and the children dress up.

frases.es: Por la mañana las personas más animadas participan en un concurso y luego sale la carroza del pueblo.
frases.en: In the morning the liveliest people take part in a contest, then the village float sets off.

frases.es: Es costumbre que los vecinos cenen juntos en la calle.
frases.en: It is the custom for neighbours to have dinner together in the street.

frases.es: La última noche se suele bailar hasta que empiezan los fuegos artificiales.
frases.en: On the last night people usually dance until the fireworks start.

frases.es: Mucha gente que vive fuera vuelve al pueblo solo para las fiestas.
frases.en: Many people who live away come back to the village just for the festival.

opciones.de: Disfrazarse de means to dress up as, and it always takes de.

opciones.la luna de miel: La luna de miel is the honeymoon, the trip a couple takes after the wedding.
opciones.la verbena: That is a night party at a festival.

bloques.pregunta: Complete: it is the custom for neighbours to dine together.
bloques.frase: Es costumbre que los vecinos ___ juntos.

opciones.cenen: Es costumbre que takes the subjunctive.
opciones.cenan: After es costumbre que, the subjunctive.
opciones.cenar: Cenar is an infinitive; es costumbre que takes the subjunctive, cenen.

opciones.viernes 13: Friday the 13th is also feared in many countries; martes y trece is the familiar Spanish tradition.

bloques.texto:
**The app cannot check this part.** For the writing, please use pen and paper. For the speaking, say it out loud and, if you can, practise with a native speaker or a teacher who can correct you.

**Write (100–120 words).** Describe a tradition or a superstition from your country and what you think of it.

**Speak (about 2 minutes).** Explain aloud to a foreigner a festival in your country: its origin, what people do and what they eat.
